feed.title: Depledge Lab
feed.subtitle: DepledgeLab focuses on understanding how human herpesviruses persist following infection and how this is influenced by different aspects of RNA biology. Here, exciting web-lab, high performance computing bioinformatics and supportive colleagues meet to create new research.

entry.title: Visiting Scientist
entry.content:
Visiting Scientist Alert

We are delighted to welcome Dr. Natalia Guminska to the lab. Natalia is a postdoc in the Andrzej Dziembowski’s lab in Warsaw and recently obtained an EMBO Exchange grant to join the DepledgeLab for three months. As the primary developer behind Ninetails, a powerful software for analysing poly(A) tails in nanopore datasets. During her visit to the lab, she will work closely with Erik to further develop the tool and to dive into many new datasets we have been generating.

entry.title: Congratulations to Dr. Elene Loliashvili!!
entry.content:
Elene Loliashvili, Ph.D.

Today, Elene became the second PhD student to graduate from the Depledge Lab (and the first from the MHH lab)! She successfully defended her thesis entitled ‘Epitranscriptomics Regulation of Varicella Zoster Virus Infection’.

Congratulations to Elene and a big thank you to the external examiners Redmond Smyth and Luca Cicin-Sain. Thank you also to the thesis advisory committee members Abel Viejo-Borbolla and Benjamin Nilsson-Payant.

Best of all, Elene won a prize for having the best thesis!

entry.title: Celebrating endings!
entry.content:
Elene Loliashvili, Ph.D.

A tradition in the Depledge Lab is to celebrate the years we have spent with our students. Following the hand-in of her PhD thesis, we celebrated Elene’s many contributions to the lab, both scientific and personal, at a wonderful Georgian restaurant. Tarragon sodas and fantastic khachapuris kept the celebration flowing.

entry.title: A collaborative grant begins
entry.content:
DFG-NWO WEAVE grant begins!

Earlier this year, Dan and his long-time collaborator Dr. Werner Ouwendijk (Erasmus MC, Netherlands) were successful in their application for a new joint project grant supported by the DFG (Germany) and NWO (Netherlands). Now the hard work begins!

entry.title: Dan gets an award!
entry.content:
Priscilla Schaffer Memorial Award & Lecture at the 48th International Herpesvirus Workshop

Today, Dan was awarded the Priscilla Schaffer Memorial Award and gave the memorial lecture at the 48th International Herpesvirus Workshop meeting in Portland, Oregon. This prestigious award recognizes is awarded on an annual basis and is given to an early career scientist who has demonstrated significant contributions to the advancement of research on herpesviruses.

Unfortunately, Dan suffered a nasty back injury a few days ago and was unable to attend the meeting in person. He therefore gave the memorial lecture by recorded video instead. The lecture was entitled ‘Regulation of the VZV latent-to-lytic switch’.
